deficient_in__tay_sachs.subject: tay_sachs
deficient_in__tay_sachs.source: Biallelic pathogenic variants in HEXA lead to absent or reduced activity in β-hexosaminidase A, a lysosomal hydrolytic enzyme required for the breakdown of ganglioside GM2 in neurons. ... The alpha chain is encoded by HEXA; the beta chain is encoded by HEXB. Deficiency of HEX A can therefore be the result of pathogenic variants in HEXA or HEXB.

accumulates__tay_sachs.subject: tay_sachs
accumulates__tay_sachs.source: Tay-Sachs disease is a progressive, lethal neurodegenerative disorder caused by a deficiency of the enzyme hexosaminidase-A that results in the accumulation of GM2 gangliosides. [...] deficiency of Hex A causes an accumulation of the gangliosides up to toxic levels, especially in the neurons.

inherited_as__tay_sachs.subject: tay_sachs
inherited_as__tay_sachs.source: This condition is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern, which means both copies of the gene in each cell have variants.

deficient_in__gaucher.subject: gaucher
deficient_in__gaucher.source: Gaucher disease (GD) is caused by deficient glucocerebrosidase activity and the resultant accumulation of its undegraded substrate, GL1, and other glycolipids. ... GBA1 encodes glucocerebrosidase (also known as glucosylceramidase)

accumulates__gaucher.subject: gaucher
accumulates__gaucher.source: The lysosomes in the macrophages of patients with Gaucher disease become progressively enlarged and filled with undigested glucocerebroside.

inherited_as__gaucher.subject: gaucher
inherited_as__gaucher.source: Gaucher disease (GD) is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner.

inherited_as__phenylketonuria.subject: phenylketonuria
inherited_as__phenylketonuria.source: This condition is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern, which means both copies of the gene in each cell must have a variant to cause the disorder.

deficient_in__pompe.subject: pompe
deficient_in__pompe.source: PD is caused by a partial or total deficiency of acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA), which induces glycogen storage.

accumulates__pompe.subject: pompe
accumulates__pompe.source: Pompe disease (OMIM: no. 232300) is a rare metabolic myopathy characterized by acid alpha‐glucosidase deficiency caused by disease‐associated variants in the acid alpha‐glucosidase (GAA; EC 3.2.1.20) gene. ... As a consequence, glycogen cannot be degraded and accumulates in the lysosomes.

inherited_as__pompe.subject: pompe
inherited_as__pompe.source: Pompe disease is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner.

deficient_in__lesch_nyhan.subject: lesch_nyhan
deficient_in__lesch_nyhan.source: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome results from deficiency of hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HGPRT).

accumulates__lesch_nyhan.subject: lesch_nyhan
accumulates__lesch_nyhan.source: Lack of the enzyme causes an increase in guanine and hypoxanthine, which eventually gets converted into uric acid. ... Although hyperuricemia is typically present at birth, the only clinical presentation in the early days of life could be orange-colored crystals in the diapers.

inherited_as__lesch_nyhan.subject: lesch_nyhan
inherited_as__lesch_nyhan.source: This condition is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern. The gene associated with this condition is located on the X chromosome, which is one of the two sex chromosomes.

accumulates__von_gierke.subject: von_gierke
accumulates__von_gierke.source: The deficiency of G6Pase (in GSD 1a) or G6PT (in GSD 1b) leads to an accumulation of glycogen in tissues, including the liver, kidneys, and intestines.
